paragraphs.text: Zapier MCP plugin for Deepseek Harness (DSH)
# dsh-zapier-mcp
**Connect your hosted Zapier MCP server to DeepSeek Harness — paste one token in Settings, and Zapie
r's tools become agent tools in every session.**
**MIT** · **DSH 0.2.x** · **Node ≥ 22.19** · **No build step**
## Why
Zapier's hosted MCP server exposes your connected apps behind a single endpoint. Wiring that endpoin
t into a harness usually means editing config files and restarting, and it usually means leaving a s
ecret lying in YAML.
This bundle does neither. It adds one row to a DSH profile, adds a **Zapier MCP** page to the harnes
s Web UI, and stores the token where secrets belong: the profile credential store. On save it re-con
nects immediately and tells you what happened. While connected, it also briefs the model on how Zapi
er's meta-tool surface works, so the model reaches for an app you have not enabled yet instead of cl
aiming it is unavailable.
## Features
- **Hosted Zapier MCP** — connects to `https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect` with your token. No lo

cal MCP server, no bridge process.
- **Token in Settings, directly below Models** — a dedicated **Za

pier MCP** page for pasting, re-checking, and removing the token.
- **Instant verification and tool
refresh** — saving re-connects immediately; the page reports `Connected — N tools available` with th

e refreshed tool name list, or `Token rejected` with the server's message.
- **Zapier intelligence i
n the system prompt** — while connected, the plugin tells the model that the listed tools are scaffo
lding, maps Zapier's meta-tool names to their callable `mcp__<serverName>__*` names, and lists which

apps are enabled right now. See System-prompt intelligence.
- **Every session, including DS Bot** —

the row mounts at the harness root, so the tools are not session-scoped.
- **Advanced endpoint over
ride** — point the plugin at another MCP endpoint (self-hosted or a local test server) from **Settin

gs → Zapier MCP → Advanced**.
- **No build step** — plain ESM, no transpiler, no bundler; `npm test`

needs no install.
- **No token in config files** — the token lives in the harness credential store
under `credentialRef`; configuration carries only the reference name.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Version |

| DeepSeek Harness (DSH) | `0.2.x` — built and tested against `0.2.1-rc.2` |
| Node.js | `>= 22.19`

|
| Zapier account with a hosted MCP server | mcp.zapier.com |
The bundle depends on the shipped package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` at exactly `0.2.1-rc.2`, whi
ch performs the MCP connection and tool registration. When your harness version changes, that pin mu
st be raised in lockstep — see Compatibility.
## Installation
Install the bundle into a DSH profile with `dsh plugin`. The command forwards its remaining argument
s verbatim to pnpm in the profile directory, so `add`, `remove`, and `why` are the pnpm verbs:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Recommended: install from GitHub
The normal path is a GitHub spec, because the package's dependencies come with it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### The tool list is scaffolding, not the capability limit

Zapier's hosted MCP server returns a **fixed set of about 16 meta-tools** from
`tools/list`, no matt

er which apps you have connected. They are the plumbing:
discover / enable / disable / inspect, exec

ute read / execute write, list and
manage connections, `auto_provision`, `write_code_action`, skills

, feedback and
the configuration URL. It is the same list whether you connected one app or
eighty.

The real surface — 9,000+ apps — is **virtual**, and is resolved at call time.
**A missing tool neve

r means an app is unavailable.** If there is no
`mcp__zapier__<some_app>` tool listed, that is expec

ted: the model is meant to
discover and enable the action through the meta-tools.
### Compatibility

The harness decides how to compose patches; the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`
package does the MCP w

ork, and this bundle pins it at exactly `0.2.1-rc.2` to
match DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. If your DSH version

differs, the symptom is usually that
the row fails to mount or the tools never register. The fix is

to raise the pin
to the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` version shipped with your DSH release.
## How it works
The bundle is one row with two halves:

- **Host half** — `index.js`, with testable logic in
`lib/host-logic.js` and prompt text in
`lib/pro

mpt.js`. It resolves the token from the credential
service **per connection attempt** (never caching

a rotated or removed token),
reads the effective endpoint per attempt (so an override applies witho

ut a
reload), mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, and re-connects when the
credential changes or t

he page asks for a re-check. Results are published into
the volatile config fields above; the system

-prompt section is a pure read of
the same facts.
- **Browser half** — `client.js`. It registers the

`settings.section` page named **Zapier MCP**, positioned directly below
**Models**, and talks to th

e settings service to save, re-check and remove the
token and to set the endpoint override.

Both halves are mounted by the single row inserted by
`cordis.patch.yml`. See the repository files f

or the
implementation details.
## Security & privacy

- **The token is never written to this bundle or to the profile config file.**
It is stored by the h

arness credential service in `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`
(file mode `600`) under `credentialRef` (def

ault `ZAPIER_MCP_TOKEN`).
- The Settings page only ever learns **whether** the token is configured;

it
never receives the token value. The token input is a password field.
- The row config and the pro

file's Cordis patch contain only the credential
*reference name* plus the volatile runtime fields (`

status`, `toolCount`,
`toolNames`, `lastError`, `checkedAt`, `inventory`, `checkNonce`), which the
h

arness settings service writes back.
- The system-prompt section carries **app names and counts only

** — never
account ids, account titles or emails.
- The token is sent only to the effective MCP endp

oint: the configured
`endpoint`, or `endpointOverride` when you set one. If you point the override
a

t a server you do not control, your token goes there.
- Removing the token deletes the stored creden

tial; nothing else about your
Zapier account is read or cached by this bundle.
